subject: Reserve shoulder commit, on-call burst agreement and autoscale cadence for NebulaMetrics
messages:
From: Evan Turner <evan.turner@nebulametrics.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurements@nebulametrics.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: short-term production spike & burst needs (MBR launch)

Kim —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re heading into a limited public beta (MBR) the week of Apr 9 and expect a concentrated burst profile: 10–12x our baseline token throughput for ~6 hours/day for the first three business days post-launch, then gradually tapering.

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood guarantee a fast path for short-lived bursts without moving us on- or offboarding?
- What does a shoulder reserve + short-term burst commit look like operationally and on price?
- We need clear cooldowns/eviction policies and an on-call contact (for pre-warm and escalations).

Sana (procurements) is copied for procurement scheduling and any contract addendum. We’re sensitive to long-term reserved commits — prefer a small monthly reserve + controlled burst pool.

Open to a short MS Teams next week to walk the numbers.

— Evan
Evan Turner
Head of Platform
NebulaMetrics
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Evan Turner <evan.turner@nebulametrics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, procurements@nebulametrics.com
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: short-term production spike & burst needs (MBR launch)

Evan —

Appreciate the context. We can support the profile you describe with a combination of: a modest monthly reserved commit (to cover baseline + predictable shoulder), a dedicated shoulder pool that can be used for short bursts, and operational pre-warm/runbook support for the first 72 hours of the launch window.

Quick proposal (high level):
- Baseline reserve: 8 A100-equivalent GPU hours/day (monthly commit) — covers baseline latency and predictable throughput.
- Shoulder reserve pool: up to 6 A100-equivalent GPUs available for up to 12 hours/day for up to 7 contiguous days (eviction and reversion policy applied after the seven-day window).
- Burst-on-demand: ephemeral capacity beyond shoulder via our oversubscription slab (best-effort, subject to global availability) — recommended only for non-SLA-critical paths.
- Ops support: 24/7 on-call for the launch window (pre-warm 2 hours prior to the expected start) + a 2-hour cooldown window after the peak.

I attached a draft schedule and a short SLA addendum we usually use for these one-off launches (proposed-capacity-schedule.pdf, MAL-sla-addendum.docx).

Karthik — can you validate the pricing sketch? Ben — can you confirm the ops constraints / cooldown times and whether we can pre-warm KV caches at the scale Evan described?

If that sounds good I’ll schedule a short sync with your procurement and ops contacts and spin up an internal runbook.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Evan Turner <evan.turner@nebulametrics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 3 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: short-term production spike & burst needs (MBR launch)

Team / Evan —

Pricing quick sketch based on Kimberly’s proposal and your expected 10–12x spike:
- Baseline reserve (8 A100-eq/day): $18,000/mo (committed) — priced to keep your baseline latency under 150ms p50.
- Shoulder reserve: priced as a smaller reserved slab — $6,000/mo for the 6-GPU shoulder pool; includes up to 84 GPU-hours/week of shoulder usage before overage.
- Burst-on-demand (oversubscription): $0.60 / GPU-hour (on top of the reserved slab); we recommend capping oversubscription at 200 GPU-hours/day for the launch window to control cost.

A few operational notes that will impact run-rate and sizing:
- If you route latency-critical traffic through the shoulder pool we recommend an overprovision factor of 1.2x to avoid SLO slippage on p95 during burst.
- If the real traffic shape is spikier than the 6-hour window you described, the shoulder pool will need to be increased or you’ll see more oversubscription usage (higher variable spend).

I’ll add this to the draft MOP but wanted to flag that procurement will need the DocuSign-ready SLA addendum + a short exhibit that lists the exact burst caps.

Laura — can you attach the exhibit version of the addendum?

— Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Evan Turner <evan.turner@nebulametrics.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask: short-term production spike & burst needs (MBR launch)

Folks —

Operational constraints / runbook items from infra side:
- Pre-warm: we can pre-warm model caches to reach steady-state in ~25–40 minutes depending on sequence lengths and KV cache sizes. Pre-warm window of 2 hours is conservative and safe.
- Autoscale cadence: 60s evaluation window, 3x consecutive windows to trigger scale-up by slab increments. Scale-down cooldown: 15 minutes to avoid oscillation during high variance traffic.
- Shoulder slab eviction: we’ll enforce a sliding 7-day window. If shoulder is used > 84 GPU-hours/week for 2 consecutive weeks, we’ll trigger a billing/alert and recommend either raising the shoulder slab or converting usage into a temporary reserved commit.
- Preemption/oversubscription: ephemeral oversubscription runs on spot-capacity across dedicated clusters — best-effort; you should avoid routing synchronous, latency critical workflows there.

I’ve attached a short ops runbook excerpt that covers the slab eviction and escalation flow (ops-runbook-slab-eviction.md). Marcus — we’ll need an on-call rota for the launch window; can you pair with Laura on runbook signoff?

Ben Carter
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
